unverified_summary: No row on this page reaches Confirmed, and none can. Scopely runs the Golden Blitz as an in-app event with no published calendar, no press note and no permanent post, so there is no publisher record to check a date against after the window shuts. Every row therefore rests on one reputable outlet plus two fan trackers, which is tier 2 and tier 3 evidence with no tier 0 or tier 1 anywhere. Two rows carry dates the outlet and the trackers disagree on by two and three days and are marked Conflicting rather than resolved. The next occurrence is not announced by anyone: the sticker pair circulating for it comes from a community Discord poll, one tracker labels it unconfirmed and a shop site prints it as already completed. The 05:00 UTC start time comes from a single tracker and no other source states a time at all. Nothing here was observed in the app by this desk.

disagreements.item: Whether the next Golden Blitz has already run
disagreements.source_a: A sticker shop lists the expected pair in its schedule table as a completed event
disagreements.source_b: An outlet and a fan tracker both call the same pair a prediction that Scopely has not confirmed
disagreements.confirmed: Not confirmed as run. The row stays in the expected table with an Unverified status until the event is observed in the app.

disagreements.source_a: Several sources say a flat 24 hours
disagreements.source_b: Others say 15 to 18 hours, and one describes windows as short as a few hours
disagreements.confirmed: Not confirmed. Every dated window on this page spans two calendar dates, which is consistent with roughly a day but does not settle the exact figure.

disagreements.source_a: One tracker states a flat interval of 4 to 6 days
disagreements.source_b: An outlet states roughly three times a month, clustered at the end of an album and absent at the start of a new one
disagreements.confirmed: The dated table supports the second description. Gaps on record run from 3 days to 26 days, so a flat interval does not fit the evidence.

fakes.claim: Published Golden Blitz calendars listing future dates as fixed schedule
fakes.why_wrong: Scopely publishes no calendar. Every future date on those pages is a projection from past gaps, and the gaps on record vary by a factor of eight, so a projection presented as a schedule is a guess with a table around it.
fakes.origin: Sticker shops and aggregator sites that need a date on the page to rank for the schedule query.

fakes.claim: Gold sticker generators and Blitz trade bots that ask for your account name
fakes.why_wrong: A Blitz trade happens inside the app between two accounts already on each other's friend list. Nothing outside the game can place a gold sticker in an album, and a username is enough to target an account for a phishing attempt.
fakes.origin: Ad funded generator sites that rank alongside genuine event pages.

fakes.claim: Claims that any gold sticker can be traded once a Blitz starts
fakes.why_wrong: Only the two featured stickers unlock. Every other gold sticker stays locked for the whole window, and you still need a duplicate of the featured one before you can send it.
fakes.origin: Video thumbnails and short form clips that compress the rule into a headline.

changes.what: Page published with 10 dated past occurrences rebuilt from three independent lists
Next occurrence recorded as expected and unannounced after sources split on whether it had run

next_change.pattern: Occurrences cluster rather than repeat on a fixed interval. Gaps on record run from 3 days to 26 days. The short gaps land in the closing weeks of a sticker album, when several Blitz windows can run inside ten days, and the long gaps land immediately after a new album or season opens, when the event goes quiet for three to four weeks. Expect nothing early in an album and expect a burst as its deadline approaches.
